Gun criteria:
22 Long Rifle either Bolt, Pump or Lever Action. All guns must use Open Sights. 5 rounds will be used for each of the three shooting legs. 

6” targets at 40 meters

There will be designated Range Safety Officers (RSO) in place that will oversee the safety of the firing range throughout the race and will assist with any issues with firearms. 

If you are sharing a gun with someone we will figure the start times so that sharing is possible. 

Guns will be racked at the Shooting Range- NO GUNS WILL BE CARRIED ON THE RUN OR THE BIKE. 

All Rifles must be pointed in a safe direction at all times, failure to point rifle in safe direction will result in a disqualification (DQ) from the event. 

Each shooter must have Eye and Ear protection on before they touch their rifle prior to approaching the firing line.

A mandatory chamber flag is required for every firearm. Homemade one is sufficent (ie zip tie, weed eater line, etc). Must not be able to fall out while rifle is in the rack. https://i.ebayimg.com/images/g/EGsAAOSwsq1crR-w/s-l400.jpg

Rifles will only be loaded when at firing line and in shooting position with rifle pointed in safe direction and under supervision of a Range Safety Officer. All Rifles must be stored and transported with the action open (bolt to the rear) and no ammunition in the firearm unless under the supervision of the Range Safety Officer at the designated shooting position. 
5 rounds only, will be prepared in advance and inserted at the firing line. After shooting, magazines will be removed at the firing line with bolts open or a chamber flag inserted before racking gun. Tube fed magazines must have feed tube removed after shooting. Racers will be responsible for picking up and loading their own guns. 

If there is a misfire, racer must wait with the rifle downrange for 30 seconds.

Mountain bike legs- racers can get assistance from other racers but no outside assistance is allowed. Anything used for a repair must be carried by the racers. 

Summer Biathlon Format (running and shooting): Time trial format- 
30-second intervals. All running loops are different. 
2 K run loop
Shoot Prone- 5 shots
2 K run loop
Shoot Offhand (standing)- 5 shots
3 K run loop
Shoot Prone- 5 shots
.1 K run loop
Finish

Mountain Bike Biathlon Format (mountain biking and shooting): Time trial format- 30-second intervals. Three mountain bike loops, the last loop is done twice
3 K mountain bike loop
Shoot Prone- 5 shots
4 K mountain bike loop
Shoot Offhand (standing)- 5 shots
3 K mountain bike loop
Shoot Prone- 5 shots
3 K mountain bike loop- repeat of 3rd mtb loop
Finish

In each shooting leg, racer gets 5 shots. For each miss, the racer must run or ride one penalty lap (penalty laps take about 20 seconds for run and 40 seconds for mtb). Example- racer one runs/ rides LOOP 1 and arrives at the shooting range. Racer puts on safety glasses and ear protection if not already wearing it. Racer picks up his racked gun and takes his five round magazine/ container of 5 shots. Racer goes to firing line and loads gun, shoots and hits the target 3 times with 2 misses. Racer unloads gun and leaves firing line back to safety line. Re-racks gun and starts running or gets on bike. Runs/ rides to penalty lap area. Does 2 penalty laps and then continues on to LOOP 2. Comes into shooting area for second time, follows shooting procedure and gets 4 hits, one miss. Runs/ rides to penalty lap, does one lap and then continues on to LOOP 3. Comes into shooting area a third time, follows shooting procedure and gets 5 hits- Runs/ rides to penalty lap, gets to bypass penalty runs/ rides last loop to the finish.

EventNotes:
Cabot Ride the Ridges 2026 marks Year 13 of this fantastic gravel grinder, with each and every year better than the last. For returning riders, we continue to have the features that make our event Cabot RTR-special - 4 different gravel distances, beautiful views, friendly volunteers with positive attitudes, wood-fired pizza as the post-ride meal, lots of well-stocked aide stations, laughs, fun, and all to support a great cause.  We will continue to have Cabot RTR merchandise available for pre-sale, as well as day-of purchase (supplies may be limited). All proceeds from Cabot Ride the Ridges have helped to fund the Cabot Mentoring Program. We hope you'll join us at this homegrown volunteer-built gravel grinder event exploring the beauty of central Vermont gravel roads, with challenging fun, lots of smiles, and friendly faces along the way! 

Our ride has been listed as a Featured Event at gravelingcyclist.com at the following link (check it out!): http://www.gravelcyclist.com/training-rides/featured-event-cabot-ride-the-ridges-cabot-vermont-usa/  If you follow this link, you will see a number of pictures of this ride which has been dubbed "the quintessential Vermont gravel grinder event" by a past rider.

Cabot Ride the Ridges has something for everyone. We organize two classic gravel-grinder events, in our 100K and 60K routes, as well as a challenging 30K and a family-friendly 10k (which non-riders can run or walk - we've even had unicycle-riding participants).  All rides offer a fun and challenging set of mostly dirt road bike rides through the scenic landscapes and rugged terrain of Cabot, Vermont (the 100k visits a few neighboring towns as well). This is a volunteer-run event with all proceeds benefiting the Cabot Mentoring Program.

These are fully supported rides. Volunteers will man a number of aid stations along the route with snacks, power food and drinks (including Cabot-made maple syrup shots). Both the 100K and the 60K are true Gravel Grinders, with the 100K covering over 7500 ft of elevation gain and the 60K traversing over 3500 ft.  The 10K and 30K are family friendly events with incredible views. Note: there will be a last time cutoff for the Peacham Aid station supporting our 100K riders.

Post ride enjoy the best food Vermont has to offer, including wood fired pizza with local and fresh veggies and meats, a variety of Jasper Hill gourmet cheeses, Cabot Cheese, the specialty goat cheeses of Vermont Creamery, along with Cabot's own Burtts Orchard apples and cider-donuts.

Note under 12 is free. Family discount applies for 2 or more, but is reserved only for the 30k and 10k rides. 

Please visit our website at http://www.ridetheridges.com for more details, including maps and cue sheets.

EventName: Major Taylor Iron Riders Legends Ride to Montauk
EventNotes:
MONTAAAUUKKKK IS CALLING YOU BACK FOR 2026!

Alright, riders — it’s ON! The legendary Montauk Lighthouse Ride is BACK and it’s going to be EPIC. Get ready to crush 125 miles of fast, flat road from Prospect Park to Montauk with your crew flying at 19–25+ mph. This is not your average ride — it’s a high-spirited, no-turning-back adventure!

SYNC YOUR WATCHES!
Three rest stops (about every 40 miles) will keep you fueled and hydrated. If you're catching the bus back, know your pace — there's a cutoff at Bridgehampton High School, 1:30pm, to make sure everyone gets to Montauk in time! If not, you will be SAG'd. 

We’ve kept the core magic from last year and added a few upgrades to make this ride even smoother and safer. Buckle up — this message is your roadmap to glory!

REGISTRATION = EVERYTHING 

No registration, no ride, no support. Period.
Every rider MUST register — no e-bikes allowed. We’ve got tiered pricing to fit your needs and cover rising costs. This ride is insured by USA Cycling, and we follow their rules to keep everyone safe.

Unregistered riders = solo mission.
No aid stations, no SAG support, no post-ride meal, no bus ride. You’re on your own.
Registered riders get a WRISTBAND — your all-access pass to Montauk magic. No band = no service, no fun, no exceptions.

POST-RIDE GLORY BUS

Your chariot awaits! The chartered bus will return to Long Island and Prospect Park (Grand Army Plaza).
Long Island riders: You can store your bike under the bus — just bring two blankets to keep it cozy.
Seats are limited, so book early! Questions? Email us: majortaylorironriders@gmail.com

POST-RIDE FEAST

Feast like a champion! Registered riders and approved volunteers get a catered meal by Harlem’s own Chef Quie featuring Charles Pan Fried Chicken (vegetarian options too!).
No wristband = no meal

PERSONAL SAG HEROES

We salute you! Personal SAG vehicles are welcome — but you must be ready to help any registered rider, not just your crew.
SAG drivers must register (FREE!) and attend a mandatory volunteer meeting on Thursday, Sept 3 @ 7:30 PM.
You’ll get a sign for your vehicle and share contact info for smooth coordination.
Important: Registration for this category is verified to ensure it is for ride volunteers only, not for active cyclists. 

CHOOSE YOUR ADVENTURE 

Pick your package before registering:

  • $102.43 – All-In Rockstar: SAG support, aid stations, post-ride meal, and bus ride back.
  • $81.13 – SAG & Sustenance Champ: SAG support, aid stations, post-ride meal. No bus.
  • $70.48 – Grit & Glory Warrior: SAG + aid stations only. No meal, no bus.
  • $54.50 – Youth Rider (18 & under): SAG, aid stations, post-ride meal. No bus.

NO same-day registration. Wristbands are handed out the morning of the ride for pre-registered riders.
No wristband = no support. No exceptions.

BAG DROP

Drop your post-ride gear on Saturday, the day before, 11 AM–1 PM at Ride Brooklyn, 187 4th Ave, Brooklyn.
Pack your essentials (blankets, clothes, toiletries). We’re not responsible for damage if your bike isn’t properly wrapped.

THANK YOU TO OUR SUPPORTERS!

Huge love to our sponsors and volunteers:
MTIR members & friends of the club, Chef Quie with Charles Pan Fried Chicken, Deli Delight, Larry’s Freewheeling, Aim Express Shippers, and Ride Brooklyn — plus every single volunteer who makes this ride possible. You’re the real MVPs!

Questions? Hit us up: majortaylorironriders@gmail.com

#WeRideAsOne #RideOrGetDropped #MajorTaylorIronRiders

2026 MATTS ABD TT #2

Registration Details 

  • Your bib number will available at check in.
  • Participation requires an American Bicycle Racing (ABR) membership (annual or single-day). Purchase and sign the waiver here:
    American Bicycle Racing Membership
  • Race-day/on-site registration is available for an additional $10 fee.

Back for 2026: Road Bike Category 

  • Choose between a Time Trial (TT) Bike or Road Bike for all categories.
  • Road Bike Definition:
    • Drop or straight handlebars permitted.
    • No tri-bars, clip-on bars, or Spinaci bars allowed.  
    • No disc wheels; both wheels must have at least 12 spokes.
    • Maximum rim depth: 90mm.
    • Purpose: Encourages broader participation by leveling the playing field for racers without TT bikes. If your bike qualifies for a road race or criterium, it’s eligible here.

Event Resources 

 

  • race flyer coming soon!!!!

Awards/Prize List

  • MATTS Points (contribute to season-long overall prizes)
  • Medals: Top 5 in each category.
  • Fastest Times of the Day (Cash Prizes):
    • Overall: 1st - $50, 2nd - $30, 3rd - $20

    • Women: 1st - $50, 2nd - $30, 3rd - $20

       

Location & Logistics 

  • Check-In Address: Route to 225 Pearl St, Maple Park, IL 60151 (Lions Park)
  • Parking: After checking in, please do not park around Lions Park.  Please park on Maple Park Road, west of W County Line Road.
  • Course Description:
    • Start line: Start line is on Washington Street in between Kane St. and Maiden Lane, on the north side of Lions Park.  Course starts heading east on Washington St. and turns left (north) on Broadway St.  Follow Broadway as it curves right (east) and turns into Thatcher. Follow Thatcher as it bends back north to Beith Road.  Turn right on Beith Road and proceed approximately .8 miles to turnaround. Turnaround and reverse course to finish which is on Thatcher, approximately .4 miles before the start line.
    • Length: 7.36 miles, flat, fast “S” shaped course with a couple gentle bends.
  • Strava Segment (Note: Subject to change due to road conditions on race day.)

Safety & Guidelines 

  • The course is open to traffic—exercise caution, especially at intersections, and ride on the right side.
  • A rear red blinking light is highly recommended.
  • Respect our host community:
    • Leave the site cleaner than you found it.
    • Keep noise levels low.
    • Use provided Porta Potties.

Share Your Experience 

  • Send photos to: midamericatimetrialseries@gmail.com
  • We’d love to share them with the MATTS community!

Questions? 

  • Email: nsrgthakkar@gmail.com
  • Phone: Jason Bambalas, 630-465-3535

EventNotes:
The Landmine Classic is a premier mountain bike race on the South Shore of Boston run by the Friends of Wompatuck State Park, Bikebarn Racing, and SE Mass NEMBA.  We offer many different race distances in order to welcome as many people into competitive mountain biking as we can, including 25-mile, 12.4-mile, 5.75-mile, and 3.3-mile single-lap courses, plus we offer a free Little Racers Quarter Mile on a wooded course (i.e. not the parking lot).  At Landmine, you get to define what an epic ride is for you. We look forward to seeing you again this year! More information about the race, course, results from past years, etc. can be found at landminemtb.com.

Please note that racing age for this event is as of December 31, 2026.

Registration will close once that cap for the event is reached. Don't delay in registering! There are also price increase on July 1st and August 1st.

No e-bikes.

What makes Landmine awesome?

  • The course            
    Almost entirely on singletrack, this race showcases a great deal of what Wompatuck has to offer.  Originally the property of the Wampanoag Tribe, in 1655, Chief Josiah Wompatuck, leader of the tribe, deeded the land (now called Hingham, Norwell, Scituate, and Cohasset), to the settlers from England. During the race you will see a variety of trail situations as well as many of the historic features of the park from when this land was used as grazing grounds in the 1800s and a military compound from 1941-1962.  Over the 3.3, 5.75, 12.4, or 25 miles, you will encounter rocks, roots, berms, pavement (minimal), fast and slow trails, etc. Although your head will likely be down and you may miss it, you will also be riding by old bunkers, blasting walls, railway beds, and stone walls.  This course takes you through the best of New England mountain biking!            
     
  • The crowd            
    The Landmine Mountain Bike Classic attracts over 650 racers.  Also, since we have single-lap courses, we're able to put everyone on it at once.  Thus, our mass starts generate a lot of crowd enthusiasm!  We also run a variety of legitimate race options for kids, including a free Little Racers Quarter Mile and also options for a real chip-timed race for even kids as young as 5. Our Little Racers course is a closed-circuit loop near our main staging area and is open all day for families to enjoy.            
     
  • Something for everyone          
    We are a family-friendly race that offers numerous course distances and class options in order to welcome as many people into competitive mountain biking as possible. We believe that all attendees should have an equal opportunity to participate in our event regardless of their race, color, religion, disability, age, gender identity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic status, or national origin. We hope to create a safe and welcoming space for athletes, volunteers, and spectators from different backgrounds, identities, and abilities at our event. We do not tolerate harassment or intimidation and anyone doing so will be asked to leave the event and will be reported to race officials. We look forward to growing the cycling community with you.        
     
  • Our volunteers            
    We put a lot of effort into making sure your day in Wompatuck is excellent and we strive to bring a level of professionalism to Landmine uncharacteristic of events run entirely by volunteers.  All year long we have volunteers maintaining and repairing trails with Landmine in mind.  Our feed zones have enthusiastic staff.  Since we are a single-lap race, it also takes numerous volunteers to mark our entire 25-mile course plus the various extensions.  Our parking team will also have you parked quickly and with ease.  And, our registration team is so good you'd almost think they're professionals.              
     
  • 18 & under are half price or more!            
    We strive to strike a balance between making sure this race is affordable for families and a good value, while not forgetting that all our proceeds benefit Wompatuck State Park. 
     
  • All proceeds benefit the Friends of Wompatuck State Park        
    The Friends of Wompatuck work in partnership with DCR to maintain and improve Wompatuck. We are a group of volunteers (predominantly mountain bikers!) who build and maintain bridges, clip trails, invest in maintenance equipment, and so much more! You can learn more about us at friendsofwompatuck.org.  

Directions

Wompatuck State Park is located in Hingham on Boston's South Shore.  Once you reach the park entrance you’re still about 10 minutes from being at the race.  Make sure you leave this extra time beyond what mapping programs and GPS’s indicate.

  • Navigating via GPS?  Type 204 Union Street, Hingham, MA into your GPS and it will get you into the park.  You then follow the signs to the start of the race.  Warning: some GPS’s still send you to a wrong (locked gate) entrance if you just select Wompatuck State Park. 
     
  • From all directions: Rt. 3 to Exit 14 (Rt. 228). Follow Rt. 228 North approximately 5 miles to Free Street on the right. Turn right onto Free Street and go one mile to the park entrance on the right (Union St).  Follow the signs to the race course.

FAQs

Can I register on race day?

There is no day-of registration, except for the Little Racer's Quarter Mile (which is free, and ideal for balance bikes or up to 20" bikes). This is not flexible.

What if I registered and need to drop out?

Contact the race directors at landmineclassic@gmail.com. It is helpful for us to know. However, registration fees are non-refundable. We are a non-profit and this event is 100% volunteer run, so please consider it a donation to the Friends of Wompatuck. This is true regardless of injury, failure to adequately train (you can change your distance, if needed), sudden schedule conflicts, or any other reason, no matter how valid. You can also not move your registration to a future year or transfer it to another rider.

Can I transfer my registration to a friend?

Registration/Race Bibs are non-transferable.

What's the difference between Cat 1 Open and Cat 2?

Both categories are doing 25 miles, but Cat 1 racers will be doing so at a much faster pace. Typically, a Cat 1 racer is targeting a finish time between 2 to 3 hours (~10 mph), while a Cat 2 racer is pacing to a 3-4 hour (~7 mph) finish time.

What's a Feed Zone and where are they located?

A Feed Zone has water, Gu brand products, first aid supplies, and some bike repair tools/tubes/pump. This is also staffed by volunteers who will cheer you on as your pedal past it. There are two Feed Zones on the course: Feed Zone 1 is 5.6 miles into the race and Feed Zone 2 is on the 25-mile course, located at mile 10.8, and Feed Zone 3 is at mile 22.5. Cat 4 (5.75 miles) and Cat 5 (3.3 miles) do not pass through any feed zones. Cat 3 (12.4 miles) only passes through Feed Zone 1. 

How do I know where to go on the course?

You will not need to do any self-navigating of the course. The Landmine is always well marked. When racing, you will follow the split signs that MATCH YOUR NUMBER PLATE'S COLOR. These are the color schemes by distance:

  • Pro/ Cat 1 / Cat 2 = Orange (25 miles)
  • Cat 3 = Blue (12.4 miles)
  • Cat 4 = Green (5.75 miles)
  • Cat 5 = Red (3.3 miles)

When you come to a course split, we’ll have a marshal on hand to help remind you which way to go. However, it will help the marshal if you already know what you’re looking for.  Below is an example of the signage at one of the course splits. 

Are e-bikes allowed?

No e-bikes are allowed as part of the race.

EventNotes:
Connecticut Valley Century Ride – A Scenic & Meaningful Cycling Event!!

Join us for the Connecticut Valley Century (COVAC)—an exciting and rewarding ride through Massachusetts, New Hampshire, and Vermont. Whether you're a seasoned cyclist or a casual rider, choose from four scenic routes: 100, 75, 50, or 25 miles.

  • Date: Sunday, September 13, 2026
  • Start Time: 7:00 AM

Explore the Beauty of the Connecticut River Valley

Riders will traverse rolling terrain, passing farmland, waterfalls, and a charming covered bridge over the Green River near Greenfield, Massachusetts. The routes follow the West bank of the river to Brattleboro, Vermont, then cross into New Hampshire before returning along the East bank through picturesque landscapes.

Ride for a Cause

Organized by the Rotary Club of Amherst, this all-volunteer event supports the Amherst Rotary Good Works Fund, which provides local scholarships and funding for charitable programs throughout Hampshire County.

Fundraise for a Cause Through Cycling!

Do you have a favorite local charity you’d love to support? Now you can!

We are a proud host of the Special Olympics Massachusetts Extra Mile Cycling event for Massachusetts. Last year, Kevin’s Krewe 2025 made an incredible impact—31+ riders and 330+ donors raised $46,107.00 for Special Olympics Massachusetts Extra Mile, using the COVAC supported ride platform.

Join the movement—on your own terms!
Fundraising is completely optional—you can participate in the ride just for the joy of cycling or take it a step further by supporting a cause close to your heart. Here’s how:

  • Register for the COVAC Ride.
  • Ride solo or with a team—you decide how you participate.
  • If you choose to fundraise, all donations can go directly to the charity of your choice or to the Rotary Club of Amherst Good Works Fund.

The Rotary Club of Amherst Good Works Fund is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization, meaning all donations made directly to the Rotary Club of Amherst Good Works Fund are tax-deductible.

Whether you're riding for a cause or simply for the experience, you’ll be part of an unforgettable event. Let’s ride, make memories, and create positive change!

Get Involved & Spread the Word

Share the ride with your friends on Facebook (link at bottom of the page).
Interested in joining the Rotary Club? Learn more about our mission [on our website].

Since its founding in 1985 by the Franklin-Hampshire-Freewheelers Cycling Club, COVAC has promoted cycling in the Connecticut Valley while making a lasting impact on the community. In 2007, the Rotary Club of Amherst took the helm, continuing this meaningful tradition.

Register Now & Secure Your Spot! – Sign up today and challenge yourself on a beautiful ride through the Connecticut River Valley.

Your registration fee covers:

Complimentary Beer, courtesy of Four Seasons Wine and Liquor of Hadley.

Arrive during the designated times and start your ride when you're ready—there are no mass starts!

  • BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series rules available at https://www.superseriescx.com/

Warmups: The course will be open for inspection and warm-up approximately 15 minutes prior to each event. Warming up on the course during an event is strictly prohibited and will not be tolerated. DQ & forfeiture of entry fee will result. ABSOLUTELY NO RIDING IN THE PARKING LOT. We will have a designated warmup area.

Staging: all riders will be staged on the grid by bib number.  

  1.  Riders will be assigned bibs in order of their overall ranking on CrossResults.com as of the close of registration.
  2. Riders who are unranked on CrossResults will be assigned bibs in the order of their registration.
  3. All categories that award SuperSeries points may reserve the first four spots in the third row for promoter's discretion call-ups.

Those categories consisting of only category 5 men or category 4/5 women are staged strictly by order of registration. All race day entrants will be staged behind the pre-registered riders, and are not entitled to any special consideration based on to their Super Series points or CrossResults ranking. Full staging details are at https://www.superseriescx.com/.

Results: BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series races are electronically timed by Insight Timing Services. The protest period is a firm 15 minutes from the announcement that results have been posted. Racers are also reminded to make sure their team name is correct in both their USA Cycling profile and their BikeReg profile.  Results will be uploaded with the Club & Team affiliations shown in the rider's USA Cycling profile.

Pit: There will be one double-sided pit on the course. Please remove your equipment immediately following your race to make room for others.

Course Description: The course utilizes the beautiful farmgrounds of Vanish Brewing, with a balance of pavement, grass, dirt paths, double track, and a good amount of elevation gain; bring those climbing legs!

Spectating: The course has great sight lines and many opportunities for spectators to get a great view of the action. With a full service brewery and food onsite, great ready to enjoy a full day of racing for the whole family! A central announcer will be located near the Start/Finish. 

Registration, Entry Fees, & Licensing:  all registration and payment for this event, including race day registration, will be conducted through BikeReg.  Addtional entries are offered at $20 ($25 on race day) when purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart.  If the entries are purchased separately during the pre-registration period, contact us for a partial refund; on event day a coupon code will be made available at the day-of registration table to achieve the same discounted price.  Entry fees will increase to $50 for adults and $25 for Juniors for race day registration, to reflect the day-of surcharge.  There will be no in-person sales at the event -- register online, either at home before coming out or on your phone at the event.  You MUST present your racing license (if you have one) or 1-Day receipt in order to be issued a bib, and you should also be prepared to show your confirmation email.  In order to expedite your entry, make sure you have completed the online waiver before approaching the day-of registration table.

This page will re-open for day-of registration by 6 AM; check-in will open by 7 AM.  Check-in and registration for all races will close 15 minutes prior to the scheduled start of the race.  There will be no exceptions made to this rule -- plan to show up timely for the race you want to enter.

Any current National Cyclocross Champions shall be granted free entry, but must wear their national jersey in the class in which it was won.

A USA Cycling racing license is required for entry.  Riders who do not provide a USAC Annual racing license # at registration will be assessed an additional $15 for a Beginner 1-Day license.  This license is valid for entry only in fields that are open to Novice Men, Women, or Non-Binary riders.  For all other fields, you must present proof of an active USAC racing license (or a printed Authorization to Ride) showing your Cyclocross category and Racing Age.

Mr. Thomas was also the former owner of Lilypons Water Gardens, which was started by his grandfather in 1917. Indy Cycloplex Collegiate Invitational – Track Cycling at the Major Taylor Velodrome

ALL COLLEGIATE VARSITY AND CLUB TEAMS ARE INVITED. Alumni that carry an active USA Cycling License are welcome to race as well. 

This is not a championship event and medals/prizes are not on the line. The spirit of this event is simply to make use of the rain out day that traditionally does not get used. Due to the nature of the potential rainout day, some teams/clubs will not be traveling home until Monday and this event will provide an opportunity for collegiate track riders to race in events not typically offered at the Collegiate National Championships. The aim of the day is to provide another opportunity for collegiate teams/clubs/athletes/coaches to get together at the velodrome and promote the community of collegiate cycling. Riders are asked to ride within their limits and to recognize the scope of the event, this is a grassroots style event where competition is friendly and top sportsmanship towards your fellow competitors is expected. 

 

In the event that the USA Cycling Collegiate National Championship is required to use Sunday as a race day for championships, the Indy Cycloplex 2026 Collegiate Invitational  will be cancelled and all riders will be refunded their entry fees. 

 

The Indy Cycloplex Collegiate Invitational brings the excitement of collegiate track racing to the historic Major Taylor Velodrome for a day of fun competition and campus pride. Student-athletes from across the country will battle it out in a dynamic race program featuring:

  • Keirin – A fast-paced sprint showdown where riders draft behind a motor before unleashing their final explosive kick.
  • Chariot Race – A single-lap dash where only the quickest start and sharpest positioning wins.
  • Elimination Race – Tactics and endurance collide as the last rider across the line each lap is pulled until only one remains.
  • Tempo Race – A test of consistency and grit where points are scored lap after lap, rewarding the smartest strategies and strongest legs.

Adding to the excitement, coaches will also take to the track for a special 1km Time Trial, showcasing their speed and giving their athletes a chance to cheer them on from the infield.

This unique collegiate showcase celebrates the spirit of cycling, competition, and community in the world of collegaite cycling . Whether you’re a racer, alumni, coach, or spectator, join us at the Indy Cycloplex to experience the energy of track cycling at one of the nation’s premier velodromes.

 

Category restrictions

Keirin: Women - 1/2/3, Men - 1/2

Chariot: Open to all categories

Tempo: Open to all categories

Elimination: Open to all categories

Coaches Kilo: Limited to Coaches of a Collegiate Team / Club. 

Requirements to race: Similar to that of the USA Cycling National Championship, participants are expected to have raced several track days before racing at the Collegiate Invitational. This event is not for collegiate points and does not count for anything; teams may enter as many or as few riders as they wish. Alumni wishing to race, in addition to the race entry fee, are encouraged to make a donation towards their alma mater prior to race day. 

All current collegiate racers, alumni, and coaches, that are registered to race must wear a collegiate cycling jersey from your institution. Bonus kudos for coaches/alumni that wear a jersey from the years you raced collegiately.

The Ride for Unity was a historic cross-country cycling journey organized by Black Leaders Detroit to promote economic justice, entrepreneurship, and unity. The ride covered approximately 1,645 miles from Tulsa's historic Greenwood District (Black Wall Street) to Wall Street in New York City, beginning on May 31, 2025, and concluding in early July.

Linda Jackson and Osborne Celestain, Jr. represented Tulsa on this landmark ride as members of the partnership between the Community Light Foundation, the Major Taylor Cycling Club of Oklahoma, and Black Leaders Detroit. How does Relay Cross work? You and a partner take turns racing laps around the cyclocross course, tagging each other at the end of each lap. It's really that simple. It is the most laid-back, low-pressure introduction to cyclocross and the cyclocross community! 

Relay Partners: Don't have a Relay Cross race partner to race with? Please let us know, and we will help you find a race partner! There are co-ed, men's, women's (W/F/T), juniors, and master's (35+) races, so there is something for everyone, and there are opportunities to race multiple times throughout the day.

Bicycles: You can use a cyclocross bike, mountain bike, gravel bike... whatever bike you think will get you through the grass, dirt, and gravel on the cyclocross course. You can share a bike with your race partner or each race your own bikes. Don't have a suitable bike??? Big Marsh proposes a good selection of bike for rental!

Relay Roulette Charity Race: As part of Relay Cross we have a fundraising race, Relay Roulette, where two riders are paired together at random for the race and all the entry fees ($10/rider) are donated to a Chicago-area cycling non-profit as chosen by the race's winning team. Since 2016, we have raised over $4,500 through Relay Roulette for local cycling non-profits like West Town Bikes, Blackstone Bicycle Works, Experimental Station, and the Northbrook Cycling Committee, which oversees the programs at the Ed Rudolph Velodrome. If you sign up to race any of the Relay Cross races, you are eligible to register for the Relay Roulette race for just $10.

COVID-19: Please remember that COVID-19 is still a public health issue and should be treated as such. Riders should not join, and will not be allowed to remain at, team events if sick or symptomatic (with cough, shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, fever of 100.4° F or above, chills, muscle pain, headache, sore throat, new loss of taste or smell, or other COVID symptoms). Sick or symptomatic riders are encouraged to seek a COVID-19 test at a state or local government testing center, healthcare center, or other testing locations, and follow guidelines for self-isolation. 

Questions: Have any other questions? Please reach out and let us know!

EventName: Tour de Taco, a Riverside Racing Production
EventNotes:
TOUR DE TACO 2026

Howdy!

The Tour de Taco is a 45-mile dirt-trail-road adventure ride through some of the North Shore’s finest trails and back roads. This epic tour through eleven different North Shore towns is a self-guided adventure (read: extra tubes, at least 40psi, water, food) so make sure you download the route to your Garmin. 

 

Check out the route, it’s one big hot pepper!

The first side of the pepper is smooth and fast power line leaving Newburyport and heading towards the canal in the southern point of Wenham.  We've removed Georgetown Center and the sketchy bridge etc. and instead will go through GTRSF and Cleveland Farm.  Mostly smooth but some singletrack.

The riders will descend into Patton Park just past the half-way point where they find an oasis of hydration and nutrition selections.

The second half of the tour will cover: Appleton Farms, Pingree, Winthrop St., Willowdale, Ipswich and hit the power line back to the bike path and Riverwalk Brewing for burritos & brews!

The purpose of this ride is to promote the wonderful world of adventure riding while supporting the elder generation of racers.  All proceeds from this event will benefit the Riverside Racing Senior Development Team; funds will go directly towards their race entry fees and travel expenses.  

Ride is limited to 150 riders.

Riders meet at Riverwalk Brewing at 40 Parker St in Newburyport, MA. Ride rolls out at 10:00 AM.

45 miles. CX bikes preferred. MTB is fine. 

Expect 3+ hours.

$75 includes your choice of chicken, pork or sweet potato burrito,and a pint glass to fill with your choice of beverage* post-ride. *first one's on us!

Riverwalk will, of course, have lots of refreshing bevvies and cold beer on tap!

EventNotes:
SAMBA BASH Rattling Creek Mountain Bike Festival

September 17 - 20, 2026

THE BASH IS ON!

REGISTRATION FEE INCREASES BY $10 after SEPTEMBER 4.

The BASH at Muckelratz is a rain or shine non-competitive mountain bike weekend in the Weiser State Forest on the Rattling Creek Trail system. SAMBA holds the event to generate funding to pay for the upkeep and expansion of the Rattling Creek IMBA Epic. Be sure to click “SHOW ALL NOTES” and scroll to bottom of page to review all details!

 

CLICK HERE TO VOLUNTEER

WE NEED YOUR HELP! SEEKING VOLUNTEERS, RAFFLE DONATIONS, CASH SPONSORS, DEMO BIKES, MOBILE BIKE MECHANICS. Anyone who commits to volunteering during the event will receive a discount code! If interested in helping make this event a success, please use the link above to sign up through SignUp Genius or send an email to events@sambabiker.com. SAMBA Staff, please be sure to check your @samba.com email account for discount code, contact events@sambabiker.com if you did not receive code.

 

Event Details:

  • Rattling Creek is classic Central PA Rock Garden riding. This is not a beginner mountain biker event, but it is not a race either. The trails are challenging but great riding can be had for most ability groups.
  • For a map please visit: Rattling Creek Trail System. It is also recommended that you download the Trailforks Rattling Creek (IMBA Epic) route to your mobile device in advance.
  • Camping is primitive with portable toilets, outdoor shower facilities and no hook-ups. We have very limited electric connectivity if needed for medical devices. The camping is in and around the main field at camp and the roads in and out are not paved.
  • Win raffle items donated by our awesome sponsors (must be 18+ and CASH ONLY $$$)!
  • Quiet hours at the Camp are strictly from 11 PM to 8 AM. This isn't just a rule; it's a township ordinance put in place because of noise complaints from neighbors. Breaking this rule could result in fines or even the permanent closure of The BASH for next year.
  • Please pack out anything you bring in to help keep our costs down!
  • HELMETS and WAIVERS are required on all groups rides due to our insurance regulations.
  • The event is only canceled due to extreme weather so come prepared for whatever we have.

Additional FAQs:

  • Are there beginner rides in Rattling Creek? There really are no true beginner rides. All the trails are technical and have rock gardens, significant elevation changes, and no easy way out except to try and make the ride. There is often no cell service on most of the trails so you still have to make it out pretty far to even get support.
  • Do I need to register in advance? Pre-registration via BikeReg is preferred. Even if you want to wait until Friday or Saturday to register, please use BikeReg. We prefer not to have to deal with cash and having the correct amount of change on hand.
  • Why is there no family rate? Families are welcome to come, but the this event is all about riding the IMBA Epic Rattling Creek Trail System. Dinner on Saturday is included in the price as are the facilities and rental of the campground.
  • What is the Saturday dinner menu? We will be ordering pizzas with various toppings and subs from the local JoJo's.
  • What about breakfast? Free coffee and bagels available (until we run out) from 730-930am in bunkhouse on Fri and Sat morning (self-serve).
  • Where is the schedule of events? A schedule will be available at the SAMBA tent. Schedule is subject to change, so please verify the latest information on event day.
  • Is water available at camp or do I need to bring my own? Yes water is available at the bunkhouse.
  • What if I am arriving late in the evening? Please check-in the next morning at the SAMBA tent. You can park anywhere within Camp Muckelratz.
  • Are dogs allowed? Yes, well-behaved dogs are permitted ON LEASH! Please ensure your dog is not a nuisance and is not aggressive toward other dogs or people. Also, be responsible and pickup after your pet to keep the area clean for everyone.
  • Is camping permitted on Sunday night? We don't rent Camp Muckleratz past Sunday at 1pm, which is when everyone must leave Muckleratz. You may camp in the state forest at the free campsites, you just have to reserve them, see Weiser State Forest website.
  • What if I want to camp but don't plan on participating in SAMBA activites/rides? We ask that you still register and pay for admission to the event since we need to cover the cost of the campground and portable toilets. If you do not wish to pay the event fee, you may camp in the state forest at the free campsites, you just have to reserve them, see Weiser State Forest website.
  • Are generators allowed? No, generators are not allowed.
  • Are ground fires allowed? No, ground fires are not allowed.
  • What is the address of Camp Muckelratz? 801 Deitrich Rd, Halifax, PA 17032. GPS Coordinates: 40.5412856,-76.7773905
  • What is the address for Lykens Glen Park? Glen Park Rd, Lykens, PA 17048 GPS Coordinates: 40.5622509,-76.6990354
  • Where can I learn about future SAMBA Events, Group Rides, and Trail Work Days? Please be sure to follow us on Luma(click SAMBA Rider - Join and also the Follow button) to get updates about future events!
  • Where should I park if I'm coming for Saturday only and not camping overnight? You can park at the entrance to Camp Muckelratz, see picture below. If this parking area is full, you can also park at the Snowmobile Lot White Oak Rd, Halifax, PA 17032 GPS Coordinates: 40.544711, -76.758519.

FAQ:

I've never ridden a mountain bike or I'm pretty new, can I come?

Absofreakinlutely! We invite ALL levels of riders to come and participate. When you sign up we have you fill out a questionnaire to place you in a group based on your skill level. We have had women start out in the beginner groups and now coming into year 3 we have seen them advance to the higher groups, which is super exciting!

If I need a bike can I rent one?

Yes! See above we're working with none other than the amazing Brown County Bikes!

Do I have to camp with everyone?

No you do not, you can stay wherever you like! We always give that option for people who want to camp on site with us but we are happy to give you other recommendations on places to stay - sometimes there are cabins or rooms on site as well! Guess what you can even stay in the same building as the bike shop - Brown County Bikes, check out Brown County Barn Burner. Contact them for availability because they've blocked rooms for our group!
You can also check out the Brown County Visitor's Center website to see all accommodation options.
https://www.browncounty.com/stay/

I'm coming with my friends will I be in the same group as them?

Maybe, maybe not. While you ride with your friends all the time at home you might be best suited to be in a different group as them for our camp. It is important for us to give you the best tools and skills you need to be successful to continue riding more confidently and comfortably. Our coaches and staff are professionally trained through PMBIA or ICP, we have organized and guided hundreds of people in the outdoors since 2014 so please trust our methods to place you in a group we feel you will most excel in. If you have concerns please let us know too!
There are times once you are in your group we may need to shift you to another group but we will discuss this with you beforehand.

I have a strict diet can you accommodate me?

We can cover vegetarian, gluten free. If you have sever allergies or other dietary restrictions we due recommend bringing your own food. While we wish we could accommodate every person's request many times we are in remote locations for our camps and the caterers or food options are very limited. If you have a strict diet please sign up for the meal plan at least 30 days out so we can communicate that to our caterer.

What is the refund policy?

If you have to cancel first you can always transfer your ticket to another camp (the following year) or coaching session with Kate or Danielle to be used within a year. 60 days out full refund after that we do not offer refunds due to paying for permits, insurance, coaches, meals, etc.

Join us for the second annual Woodly's Great Gravel Adventure on Saturday, September 19, 2026! 

About the Race
Woodly's Great Gravel Adventure is presented by the Mountain State Forest Festival, one of the largest and oldest festivals in West Virginia. This year's 88th annual event will be held September 26 - October 4. The MSFF is a real cultural landmark that showcases WV in all its autumn glory. Due to the changing fall leaves and the Mountain State Forest Festival, autumn is a great time to visit the Elkins area with family and friends. Visit Mountain State Forest Festival | Elkins, WV to see all that the MSFF has in entertainment, food, and events while in town for the ride!

The race will traverse through the beautiful Cheat-Potomac District of the Monongahela National Forest. Race headquarters will be stationed in Stuart Recreation Area nestled along the banks of the Shavers Fork River. Stuart Recreation Area is 7 miles east of Elkins and was built in 1937 by CCC labor. Known to locals as Stuart's Park, the area provides great hiking trails and excellent fishing.

Woodly's Great Gravel Adventure is part of the WV Gravel series. Please visit WVGS website www.wvgravelseries.com for rules and regulations.

The majority of the race will be on gravel roads with some rail trail and paved roads mixed in. 

 

Aid Stations
2 aid stations will be along the course. The short course will pass only one aid station.  The medium and long course will go by two.  We recommend bringing appropriate fuel and drinks. Please monitor the weather and dress accordingly. Elkins weather can range from hot to snow in the autumn season.

Package Pick-Up
Package pick-up will begin Saturday, September 19 at 8:00 AM at Stuart Recreation Area in the small pavilion. (we were in the large pavilion last year, the small pavilion is a little past the large in Stuarts Recreation Area).

The Start
All riders will begin at the Small Pavilion in Stuart Recreation Area and head out of the park to Forest Road 91 and turn left on Shaver Fork Road.  All riders will continue approximately 16 miles to the first aid station.   Long, medium, short and e bike riders will start at staggered times.  Long course rides will begin at the start finish line beside the small pavilion at 9:00 AM, Medium course will begin at 10:00 AM and Short course and e bikes at 10:30AM.

Short Course
Once leaving Stuarts Recreation Area the short Course will continue along Shavers fork road which runs beside the Shavers Fork of the Cheat River until reaching the the first aid station, approximately 16 miles.  At this point you will turn and go back to Stuart Recreation Area and the finish line following the Shavers Fork road for a total of 33 miles.  Tentative course is posted here. Click here for: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/53598614?privacy_code=9FmkGxzNAnA49KPVGykAeBXJexGSZzAp 

Medium Course
The Medium Course will follow the short course until the first aide station.  At this intersection a sharp right turn will be made onto Forest Road 828 to enter the Fernow Experimental Forest.   At the intersection with Forest Road 709 a right turn will be made.  Then a slight right will be made onto Forest Road 701.  We will continue to 701 through the Fernow Forest until intersecting with Brooklyn Heights Road just East of the town of Parsons.  At this intersection a left turn will be make onto a paved road.   Brooklyn Heights Road will become Billings Avenue.  We will continue on Billings Avenue into the town of Parsons.   Billings Ave will become Railroad Ave and after a few blocks will intersect with River street.  A sharp right and then left will be made to put us on the Allegheny Highlands Rail Trail.   The Rail trail will take us through the Town of Parsons and then continue on the trail until intersecting Shavers Fork Road.  Take a left onto Shavers Fork Road.  Continue on Shavers Fork Road and it will become Clifton-Nail Run Road.  We will continue along Clifton-Nail run road until coming to the Second aid station.  At this point a left turn will be made to cross the river and intersect with Shavers Fork road.  Turn right onto Shavers Fork Road and continue to the finish line in Stuarts Park Recreation Area for a total of 48 miles.  The Course is posted here: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/53599343?privacy_code=JCHJNuC8ct14apg3jiZSMLhraOVlulDk

Long Course
The Long Course will follow the short course and medium course into the Fernow Forest.  After traveling on forest road 701 for a short ways a right turn will be made onto forest road 324 towards McGowen Mountain.  We will travel about 7 miles to the Yellow Creek trail head and turn around to return to to Forest Road 701.  We will turn right off of 324 back onto 701 and continue on the Medium course route as seen above until reaching the second aide station.   At the second aid station the Long Course will turn right and continue on Clifton-Nail Run Road until turning left on Log Lick Run road (also known as Timbucktoo Road).  Log Lick Run will intersect with Stalnaker Run Road.  A left turn will be made onto Stalnaker road.  Continue on Stalnaker Run Road until coming to the “graffiti bridge.”  After crossing the bridge continue until taking a right onto Shavers Fork Road and continue to Stuarts Park Recreation area and the finish line for a total of 75 miles.  The Long Course is posted here: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/55908392

 

 

 

 

E-Bike Route.

The E-bike route will begin at the Stuarts recreation area and head out of the park on Forest Road 91.  As soon we leave the park we will turn left onto Shaver Fork Road.  We will continue on the Shavers Fork road until reaching the “blue bridge” a left turn will be made onto Clifton-Nail Run Road.  Once crossing the bridge there will be an Aid Station.  Continue going straight until reaching Log Lick Run, at this intersection turn left.  Continue on until the intersection of Stalnaker Run Road.  A left turn will be made here.  Continuing on Stalnaker until the “Graffiti bridge," just after passing the bridge you will turn right back onto Shaver fork Road. This will bring you back to the start finish line in Stuarts Park.  The route is a total of 27 miles. Click here for:  https://ridewithgps.com/routes/56387987

 

All riders will receive a meal and t-shirt with registration and a ticket to the  Forest Festival Kickoff Party and Chili Cook-Of (scheduled from 4-8pm September 26th in Elkins).  Additional meals and t-shirts can be purchased. You must register before August 28th to get a T-shirt.

Prizes
First, second, and third finishers for male and female open riders for the long course will receive a cash prize. All winners from each category will have prize table selection.  

Lodging and Camping
Stuart Recreation Area has individual camping sites that must be reserved for tents and campers. Reservations can be made at Recreation.gov Stuart Recreation Area, Monongahela National Forest - Recreation.gov

A group campsite that accommodates 40 people tent camping is also available. This site is available first come, first serve Friday, September 18 and Saturday, September 19 for $5.00 and can be paid for day of event.

EventNotes:
Amanda and David Sheek invite you to Mammoth Lakes, the gateway to mountain adventure, for a gravel event and adventure festival to challenge the toughest of riders. The fifth annual Mammoth TUFF will take place September 19, 2026, and offers three distances so you can explore your version of TUFF. The short and medium courses will circle the famous caldera while the long course will travel through the Volcanic Tableland formed by the eruption thousands of years ago. The event is hosted by the Village at Mammoth Lakes and is part of the UCI Gravel World Series for 2026.
 

Guide: Click here to access the '26 guide 

The 2026 TUFF GUIDE is published as of Aug 25. 

Policy: 
No refunds. However, should the event be canceled due to adverse weather, natural catastrophe (forest fires included), or terrorism that threatens the safety of riders, a full refund will be issued to riders. 
Transfers allowed. Participants can transfer their registration to another participant for a $10 surcharge. 
BikeReg offers the Allianz Registration Protection to participants when checking out. This Allianz Registration Protector gives you an opportunity to get reimbursed for up to 100% of your entry if you can’t attend the event for a qualifying reason. We recommend purchasing insurance for your protection. 

Course/Routes:

Final routes will be released on the week of the event (~Sept 14). Due to the success of the ‘25 routes, you can expect the ’26 routes to be very similar. We are giving ourselves the flexibility to tweak the routes until the week of the event due to road conditions and safety factors. 
We encourage self-sufficiency with this event; however, there will be sufficient supplies and support at aid stations. Courses will be marked, but we suggest you have a computer or phone with nagivating capabilities. 

UCI Gravel World Series:

UCI Gravel World Championship qualifier categories are noted in the registration categories and those Age Groups are defined by the rider’s age on December 31, 2026. Riders in the elite category must hold a UCI license and provide the UCI ID when registering. NO license is required for the UCI Age Group categories; however, riders who qualify for the UCI Gravel World Championships and choose to race must hold a valid license issued by USA Cycling for that race. Our event grants qualification rights for the UCI Gravel World Championships for those riders finishing in the top 3 of each official category as well as those finishing in the top 25% of each official category.
Elite riders and younger age groups (19-49) will ride the TUFFEST course.
Older age groups (50-84) will ride the TUFFER course.

Adaptive TUFF:

We have Para Categories for the Short course and we will continue to run the Adaptive TUFF distance as an official route. Select Para Hand Cycle or Para Traditional Cycle in the custom questions during registration for the Adaptive Category. 

TUFF Stuff:

Registrations before July 14, 2026 at 11pm PST are guaranteed a free shirt. All registrations after July 14 will have the option to purchase merchandise from a limited inventory. Thanks for understanding and helping our order process.

If you want to order the 2026 shirt for pick-up at registration because you registered too late, you can order from our excess inventory here: https://tuffaf.net/

Want to preview our routes, learn from the best, and get some training in? Join us for our TUFF Camps around Mammoth and Bishop. More info on camps here.

EventNotes:
No Pain, No Chain 
Chainless Downhill Race on Paper Route  
September 27, 2025 
 
Get ready for a unique test of skill and strategy at the No Pain, No Chain, a chainless downhill race that challenges riders to rely entirely on momentum and technique. All participants must remove their bike chains before racing, making this an event where pumping, cornering, and line choice are more important than ever. With a couple of punchy uphill sections sprinkled in, racers will have to think fast: stay on the bike or jump off and run? 
 
Timing:  
The course will be open for practice runs during the first two hours of the day, followed by timed race runs in the afternoon. Participants may complete up to three timed runs between 12:00 and 3:00 PM, with their fastest time counting toward the final results. 
Open Practice: 10:00 AM – 11:30 AM 
Timed Race Runs: 12:00 PM – 3:00 PM  
Awards Ceremony: 3:30 PM 
 
Race Categories:  
Open/Expert (Any Age M&F) 
10 and under (M&F) 
11-18 (M&F)  
19-39 (M&F)  
40+ (M&F)  
 
Course Description:  
The course will utilize the blue square downhill trail called “Paper Route” and a newly opened trail, “Return to Sender”. These trails combine for 1.3 miles and are a mix of machine-built flow features and more natural technical sections. The trail takes riders from the top of American Express over to the bottom of the Sun Bowl lift, under the Snowbridge, before making its way to the base area.

EventNotes:
Race headquarters and staging is located at the Oatmeal Community Center, 8306 CR 336, Bertram, TX. 
 

Registration: Online registration is open and entries are fully refundable before Sept 14. A $15 late and onsite registration fee will be added after Wednesday, Sept.  16 at 5 pm. Registration closes at 6 pm on Friday, Sept. 17. There will be no onsite registration. Juniors under 19 may register at a discounted rate (subject to price increases/late fees as stated above).

No valid USA Cycling license, no race: USA Cycling licenses are being verified. Your license must match the category you seek to enter. Please address any issues before race day (USAC is closed on the weekends). Race staff will not be able to help you fix your USA Cycling license issues

Volunteers: Hosting races is only possible with the help of volunteers. As a sign of our gratitude, volunteers will receive a complimentary race entry. View the available positions for course marshals, lead/follow drivers and more at - 

 

Course: The race takes on a 13.3 mi loop beginning at the Oatmeal Community Center and heading north on FM 243. Racers will turn right on CR 321, right on FM 1174, and right again on FM 243 to complete the loop. On the finishing lap, racers will sprint for the line at the top of the hill just south of the community center. Racers are responsible for knowing their lap count. 

1 lap route - https://www.strava.com/routes/3370111538985559256

2 lap route - https://www.strava.com/routes/3370110967302608028

3 lap route - https://www.strava.com/routes/3370111853734974600

5 lap route - https://www.strava.com/routes/3494449728492462682

7 lap route - https://www.strava.com/routes/3494452314498049264
 

Feed: The feed zone will be marked and located near the finish line on FM 243. Feeding is from the right side only. Race officials will communicate about which laps the feed zone will be open. It is the racers responsibility to follow these rules. Infringements may result in disqualification. Pending available volunteers, neutral feeding may be offered.
 

Littering: Littering is strictly forbidden. Items may be discarded in the feed zone or proper receptacles only. Infringements may result in disqualification or fines. 
 

Number Pick Up and Registration: Number pick up and registration closes 30 minutes before the start of each race. Please plan to arrive at least 45 minutes before you think is necessary. Registration desk opens at 6 am at the Community Center.

Failure to follow these parking instructions or other behavior like blocking driveways, sidewalks or parking on private property will result in disqualification from the race and fines.

 

Restrooms and Changing Tents: Restroom and changing facilities are located at the south entrance to the parking lot. Public urination or uncovered changing will result in disqualification from the race and fines from the City.

The Red Bird Crest 80K and 40k will  feature an epic course with lots of rocky features, single track, climbs, and amazing descents. This course will challenge your physical fitness and your bike handling. 

Course description 80k-

The 80k course will storm out of the Peabody Trail Head into section 1-5 of the crest trail. the first major climb comes quick as you climb out of the river bottoms to the long ridges this region of Ky is known for. Enjoy some very flowy trail with some super technical rock gardens scattered throughout for the next ~10 miles. Around mi 10 you will arrive at the first SAG location. General bike tools water and race snacks, will be available. 

As you leave the first SAG stop you will have a short climb to get back to the ridge top. The next 6 mi is a very fast rolling section. This is the time to pedal hard and cover some ground. The end of this section will greet you with a technical descent. Take care of your equipment here a puncture in these big rock gardens could ruin your day. after this decent the 80k and 40k course will split. The 80k course will continue straight across the gravel road to climb up to another ridge. This next section is about 7 mi long and features some of the best riding in southeastern ky. With dozens of switchbacks and flowy trail you will have a smile on your face as you grind away. After this section you will arrive at the next SAG station ~mi 25. This is the most remote part of the race. Utilize our drop bag service at this stop, you've earned it.

 For the next ~7 mi it's time to work your way off the ridge and into the river bottoms. Expect some beautiful rock outcroppings and a few creek crossings. you will exit the crest trail onto Elijah Creek rd. Follow the signs as you cross onto HWY 66 and onto HWY 2000. These are super low traffic roads but keep a whery eye for traffic. This will be a great time to refuel for what awaits.  

Sag #3 is at ~mi 34. The best singletrack in all of Southeastern KY awaits after a quick double track climb up to the ridge. Large cliffs will provide amazing views as you grind away at this last big climb of the day. As you top this ridge congratulations its (mostly) downhill from here. If you were brave enough to pedal a longer travel bike to this point your in for a treat. Lots of rocks, tights turns, and skinny trails are instore for you till the end. with about 4 miles to go you will begin and epic decent. Lots of technical rocky turns and drops are on the menu. Don't overheat your brakes! This is a serious descent. As you exit the single track pedal across hwy 66 back to the Peabody Trailhead and cross the finish line.

Course description 40K-

The 40k course will storm out of the Peabody Trail Head into section 1-5 of the crest trail. The first major climb comes quick as you climb out of the river bottoms to the long ridges this region of Ky is known for. Enjoy some very flowy trail with some super technical rock gardens scattered throughout for the next ~10 miles. Around mi 10 you will arrive at the first SAG location. General bike tools water and race snacks, will be available. 

As you leave the first SAG stop you will have a short climb to get back to the ridge top. The next 6 mi is a very fast rolling section. This is the time to pedal hard and cover some ground. The end of this section will greet you with a technical descent. Take care of your equipment here a puncture in these big rock gardens could ruin your day. after this decent the 80k and 40k course will split. The 40K course will turn right onto Gilberts Creek and follow the river bottom to Sugar Creek. Keep an eye out for elk they often frequent these creek banks. A nice hard pack gravel road climb back up to the ridge will have your searching for traction. You will rejoin the Crest Trail with about 5 mi to go. ITS GO TIME! With a mostly downhill grade pedal hard and race back to the line.

EventNotes:
Welcome to the ShredHER DSM MTB skills clinic powered by Kilowatt Coaching! Here's what to expect:

 

WHERE:

JUNE Skills Clinics: June skills clinics will be held at the Rose Garden, 4500 Grand Ave., Des Moines, IA 50312 (go to / google the Ashworth Splash Pad)

AUGUST Skills Clinics: August skills clinics will be held at Rose Garden, 4500 Grand Ave., Des Moines, IA 50312 (go to / google the Ashworth Splash Pad)

SEPTEMBER Skills Clinics: September skills clinics will be held at Rose Garden, 4500 Grand Ave., Des Moines, IA 50312 (go to / google the Ashworth Splash Pad)

 

WHAT:

Beginner Two Hour Clinic:

This clinic will cover the foundational skills for people new to off-road riding and/or new to riding a mountain bike (flat handlebar, vs drop handlebar). 

 

15-min - Intros and Bike ABCs

15-min - Neutral/Ready Position

20-min - Bike/Body Separation - Side/Side & Fore/Aft

15-min - Braking

15-min - Shifting/Ratcheting

15-min - Climbing & Dismounts 

15-min - Descending & Dismounts

10-min - Wrap-up

 

This clinic is right for you if:

  • You are interested in getting off road, but don’t know where to begin.
  • You have not attended a skills clinic previously (or want more practice with these skills).
  • These skills are not familiar terms.
  • You want to connect with more women riding dirt.
  • You like to have fun, laugh, encourage friends, and challenge yourself.

 

Intermediate Two Hour Clinic:

This clinic will cover the foundational skills for people familiar with off-road riding and interested in advancing their MTB handling.

 

15-min - Intros and Bike ABCs

10-min - Neutral/Ready Warm up

10-min - Trackstand

20-min - Cornering

15-min - Wheel Lifts - Front & Rear

15-min - Level Lift

15-min - ¼ Punch Front Wheel Lift

15-min - Roll Down Lunge

05-min - Wrap-up

 

This clinic is right for you if:

  • You regularly ride off-road (Denman/Sycamore) and want to level up your riding.
  • You have attended a Kilowatt Coaching or other BICP based beginner skills clinic.
  • The beginner skills are familiar terms and the intermediate skills are not familiar.
  • You want to connect with more women riding at this level.
  • You like to have fun, laugh, encourage friends, and challenge yourself.

Carpenter Cross - TRIFECTA

Course Map - !BRAND NEW LOCATION! - Please look for the course map on our facebook page as we get closer to the event date!

OUR 3rd NEW VENUE THIS YEAR COMPLETES THE CARPENTER CROSS TRIFECTA

Venue

This year Carpenter Cross will take place in Chestnut Creek Park.  Of course we are staying in Horsham Township, Pennsylvania, which is located close to PA Turnpike "Exit 343 Willow Grove" and only 40 minutes from Philadelphia and Delaware. 

Like us on Facebook and get updated information ... including prizes, sponsors, and a sneak peek at the course ...  https://www.facebook.com/CarpenterCrossCX

Directions

273 Lower State Rd.
HORSHAM, PA 19044

Registration

  • Racing age is determined by your age on December 31, 2027 (not 2026)
  • Please pre-register to avoid paying $10 day-of fee
  • Registration opens @ 7:15 am and closes 15 min. before the start of each race
  • $12 for additional races
  • Mountain bikes without bar ends are ok to race

Licensing Requirements

  • USA Cycling license is required to race (Not for KIDS Race)
  • One-Day licenses will be available at the registration table: Beginner $15 | Experienced $35

Call-up Protocol

  • Order of pre-registration will be called accordingly
  • Riders MUST pre-register to be seeded
  • Staging will begin 10 minutes prior to each race

Staging 

All racers should present to the start grid 15 minutes prior to the start of their race. 

Lapped Riders
Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leaders.  Riders in danger of being lapped must yield to oncoming racers and are not to interfere with their progress or trail behind them.

Technical Pit
A double-sided pit will be marked and available approximately half way through the course. If riders enter the pit, they must make some sort of exchange or mechanical adjustment before re-entering course.

Race Results

Results will be posted after the conclusion of each race at a location designated by the race director and announced at the start line by the chief referee. After results have been posted racers will have a 15 minute protest period to resolve any discrepancies. It is the racers’ responsibility to verify their result during this 15 minute protest period. After the 15 minute protest period results will be final and will not be changed afterwards. Any further disputes must be addressed in writing via email to the riders Local Association contact.

Parking
Use the parking lot in Chestnut Creek Park.  Please park as close as possible to the vehicle next to you without leaving any big gaps. Please DO NOT park in any of the nearby neighborhoods or across the street. 

Clothing Helmets are required for all riders on bicycles, even when not actively racing (eg, while riding from the parking lot). Per USAC regulations, racers must wear a jersey with sleeves covering the shoulders. No tank tops are allowed. Race radios and earphones for playback (eg, mp3 player) are not allowed while racing.

Kids Race A fun kids race will start at 12:15 pm for kids too young to race on the real course (10 and Under).  A parent must sign the event release form prior to the race, and each kid will be given a race number. Pedal bikes or strider bikes are acceptable. All entrants will receive prizes for participation.

Food TBD

Restrooms Park restrooms will be open, as well as a couple extra porta potties located next the restrooms and near the upper corner of the main parking lot.

Race Cancellation Policy: The course is Horsham Township property. If weather conditions are such that the race would cause significant damage to the property, eg, heavy rains and water drenched grounds prior to and during the event, the race may be canceled. The race promoter will make every attempt to determine prior to race day if the race needs to be canceled, however, under extreme conditions the entire race may need to be canceled on the day of the race. Every effort will be made to hold the race, including making course modifications if necessary. If the race is canceled on the day prior to the race, notification will be sent to all pre-registered racers via email, and via the race's Facebook page. If the race is canceled prior to the event date, then registration fees, minus bikereg fees, will be refunded to those racers. 

Other than these specific weather conditions - there are NO REFUNDS!

Support

Thank you to Horsham Township  for making this race happen.  Please do your part when leaving Chestnut Creek Park and take out what you brought in.  All Horsham Township property's are drug and alcohol free so please honor the rules so we can return here next year to race.

AND A HUGE THANK YOU TO OUR SPONSORS!!!

Venue Camping — Reserved Spots Only

Camping at the venue is available in the designated CBMR parking area and is limited to 150 campers. To camp at the venue, each person must reserve a spot by purchasing it with their registration. Spots are first come, first served, so reserve early.

Venue Camping Rules

Due to increased bear activity on the mountain this season and the parking lot surface, all campers must follow these requirements:

  • Camping is permitted only in the designated camping area
  • Tents must be properly secured. If tents cannot be staked into the lot surface, weight them down well. If you use rocks from around the parking lot, return them to where you found them before leaving
  • Absolutely no food or scented items (even deodorant) may be stored in tents — this is a hard rule due to bear activity
  • If you're traveling in an SUV, wagon, truck, or similar vehicle, we strongly encourage sleeping in your vehicle as the safer option
  • No water, sewer, or power hookups are available; all vehicles must be self-contained
  • There will be portable toilets and bear proof trash containers for your use in the camping area.
  • No alcohol is permitted in the lot
  • Dogs must remain on a leash at all times
  • NO FIRES
  • Keep the camping area clean; all trash must go in the provided containers
  • All local, state, and federal laws apply
  • Highly suggest having bear spray. They do not respond to air horns.
  • A Camp Host will be on premises all weekend to answer any questions.

FREE Camping Options

Free camping is available in local camping areas and on the Western Colorado University campus. If you would like to camp on the Western campus, contact race director Jason Tullous (jtullous@western.edu) for information.

EventNotes:
Join the Bicycle Coalition of Greater Philadelphia for Roll Wit It, a Gran Fondo-style Fun Ride and Challenge benefitting the Bicycle Coalition Youth Cycling (BCYC) program. This high-impact program prepares youth ages 12-18 for success on and off the bike, supporting them as they develop healthy habits, leadership, and independence through the sport of cycling. 

When you ride Roll Wit It, you’re paying it forward — your entry fee and team fundraising goes to support the BCYC collegiate scholarship program.

About the 2026 Routes: 

  • The Whiz — a 17 mile casual loop featuring a trip through Manayunk's Main Street and one hill before the rest stop in the middle. (https://www.strava.com/routes/3509647406284203612)
  • The Whiz Wit — 38.5 mile route with local terrain, rolling hills, and shaded roads. Multiple refuel stations in Bryn Mawr, Wayne, and Conshohocken. (https://www.strava.com/routes/3509649006567552604)
  • The Works — a scenic 69.8 mile route with a few signature climbs, plus a segment of the Chester Country Trail and a dip into Valley Forge National Historic Park. Our rest & refuel partner sites will be located in Narberth, Bryn Mawr, Wayne, Phoenixville, Valley Forge park, and Conshohocken. (https://www.strava.com/routes/3504298350867027966)
  • The Pretzel – explore roughly 18 miles of Philly's MTB trails in and around Belmont.

All rides end with a family-friendly party at Sedgley Porter House, where we’ll celebrate the 2026 BCYC Athlete and Coach of the Year, and enjoy food, drink, music, yard games, and more.

Location:

Rides start and end at Sedgley Porter House near Lemon Hill in Fairmount Park.
Address: 3250 Sedgley Dr, Philadelphia, PA 19130 

Event Schedule:

7am: Check-in opens
8am: The Works departs
9am: The Wiz Wit departs
10am: The Wiz & The Pretzel departs
11:30am to 2pm: Yard party & celebration at Sedgley Porter House
1:00pm: Awards presentation for Youth Athlete of the Year & Coach of the Year

Please note:

  • Helmets are required to ride.
  • All riders are expected to have a fully functional and well-maintained bicycle (tech support will be available at ride start). Bring a flat kit!
  • All routes may be navigated with cue sheets and/or GPS routes. Both will be provided at registration and/or packet pick-up.
